policy_title: Improve Cooperation with Europe on Cross-Border Crime
stated: Improve cooperation with our European neighbours on tackling cross-border crime, such as human trafficking, the illegal drug trade, cybercrime and terrorism, including by: Working with Europol and Eurojust to develop and implement a joint strategy for dealing with cross-border threats, with the closest possible cooperation on shared priorities. Restoring direct, real-time access for UK police to EU-wide data sharing systems to identify and arrest traffickers, terrorists and other international criminals.

source.quote: Improve cooperation with our European neighbours on tackling cross-border crime, such as human trafficking, the illegal drug trade, cybercrime and terrorism, including by: Working with Europol and Eurojust to develop and implement a joint strategy for dealing with cross-border threats, with the closest possible cooperation on shared priorities. Restoring direct, real-time access for UK police to EU-wide data sharing systems to identify and arrest traffickers, terrorists and other international criminals.

bearing_set.reason: Restoring real-time UK police access to EU data systems and joint strategy with Europol/Eurojust directly affects the UK's capacity to detect, arrest and prosecute traffickers, terrorists and other international criminals — a material effect on safety and security.

Restoring UK police's real-time access to EU-wide personal data-sharing systems materially expands surveillance reach, directly bearing on the privacy/surveillance indicator under personal liberty — a non-negligible liberty cost even where the safety benefit (O5) is real.

membership_note: Classic law-enforcement pairing: the safety benefit lands on O5 and the surveillance expansion lands on O10 as a concurrent worsening; both effects are mechanistically grounded and non-negligible.
